title: Keyboard-first rollout wizard: localized microcopy, color-token fallbacks, and escapeable modal flow
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and prototype a keyboard-first rollout wizard used in the Console 'Deploy -> Rollout' flow. Goals: (1) ensure full keyboard and screen-reader operability across locales (including RTL), (2) provide robust color-token fallbacks so tenant theme overrides cannot break WCAG contrast, and (3) introduce a predictable, escapeable modal flow with clear focus-management/announcer behavior for status updates and errors. This ticket covers the design spec, edge-case prototypes, localized microcopy checks, and handoff artifacts for engineering and QA.
acceptance_criteria: All interactive elements in the rollout wizard are operable via keyboard alone (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Arrow keys where applicable)
Modal is focus-trapped while open; Escape closes and returns focus to the rollout trigger; focus return is validated in nested modal scenarios
Progress stepper is keyboard navigable and exposes the current step via aria-current or aria-selected and a readable string that is localized
Live status updates (validation, deployment progress, failures) are announced in a predictable order using aria-live regions: polite for status, assertive for blocking errors
Microcopy has been reviewed and tested for length/line-wrapping in German, Japanese, Spanish, Arabic (RTL) to prevent truncation or overlap with controls
Color token fallback table implemented: if a tenant theme token produces contrast <4.5:1 for body or <3:1 for UI accents, the system falls back to approved high-contrast mapping
Design tokens include semantic tokens for states (idle, in-progress, success, warning, error) with contrast-validated fallbacks; documented in the design token registry
High-contrast and prefers-reduced-motion OS settings are respected by the wizard (no motion-first affordances)
design_notes: Prototype variants: 1) Inline stepper with keyboard arrow shortcuts, 2) Full-screen wizard for long flows, 3) Compact modal for quick rollouts. Figma file: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/rollout-wizard-a11n
Use semantic HTML where possible (button, progress, nav) to avoid custom elements that break AT; role="dialog" + aria-modal for modal wrapper with labelledby pointing to header

Announcer order: ensure the step title is announced before any status message to maintain context for screen-reader users. Use a single aria-live region for step-specific messages and a separate assertive region for errors
Locale considerations: date/time formats in the deployment scheduling step must use Intl.DateTimeFormat and be tested in fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP, ar-SA. Avoid hard-coded month/day order in labels
Microcopy guidelines: keep action labels verb-first (e.g., 'Start rollout', 'Pause rollout'), include short helper text under toggles rather than tooltips that aren't keyboard discoverable
Contrast tooling: add a design-linting job to the tokens pipeline to run contrast checks against a snapshot of common tenant overrides
tasks: Finalize Figma comps for all three prototype variants and create a microcopy spreadsheet with translations
Create handoff spec in Confluence: keyboard flows, DOM expectations, aria-live mapping, token fallback table (https://confluence.internal/redwood/rollout-wizard-a11y)
Pair session with frontend engineers to walk through focus management and nested modal constraints (link to recording: https://zoom.us/rec/EXAMPLE)
Define Playwright e2e tests for keyboard-only journey and locale-specific snapshots; include RTL test run on ar-SA
Add contrast regression checks to the design-token CI job; produce fix suggestions when contrast < target
Usability pass with 6 participants across English, German, Arabic to validate microcopy and keyboard semantics

decisions: Adopt single-panel replaceable modal pattern (no true nested modals) to avoid double focus traps and simplify keyboard flow
Use a two-region announcer strategy: polite for progress/status, assertive only for blocking errors; step titles announced first
Introduce a documented color-token fallback table in the design token registry and wire a CI check to fail builds that would allow contrast < target
Prefer inline helper text under controls over tooltip-only explanations to guarantee keyboard and screenreader visibility
Implement a lightweight keyboard shortcut (Ctrl/Cmd+P) for Pause rollout with explicit discoverability in the keyboard shortcuts modal
